newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal says budget sustainability prime goal.
newsitem.headline: Portugal says budget sustainability prime goal.

text.p: Portugal issued on Friday a three-year economic plan predicting a halving in its budget deficit and sharp falls for inflation in 1998-2000.
The Socialist government said the plan was underpinned by a conviction that the process towards lower budget deficits, disinflation and stable currencies must be sustainable.

"The sustainability of the process ... constitutes an overriding objective," the Finance Ministry said, presenting the "Programme for Convergence, Stability and Growth" which was sent to the European Commission on Friday.

The ability to sustain the measures was necessary not only because of Portugal's commitment to being in the first wave of European Union countries to launch the single currency in 1999, but also because it was the only way to ensure economic stability, the ministry said.
"This process is essential to the defence of a state of economic stability conducive to growth and the creation of jobs on a solid basis," it said.

The ministry said that the purpose of the programme, which predicted a budget deficit of 1.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2000 down from a forecast 2.9 percent this year, was to ensure that "convergence, stability and growth" were made compatible.
The European Union has set a three percent deficit in 1997 as one of the key conditions for qualifying for economic and monetary union from the start.

"The rigour and discipline of budget policy constitute, in the view of the Portuguese government, the fundamental pillar of macro-economic stability...indispensable to consolidate the confidence of markets and encourage non-inflationary growth," the ministry said in the introduction to the programme.
Most of the numbers in the document had already been leaked to Portuguese newspapers.
The forecasts included an expected quickening in economic growth in 1997 to 3.3 percent from the three percent used to draw up the budget.
Inflation was seen easing steadily to 1.8 percent in 2000 from a forecast 2.5 percent in 1997.
